## 開篇固定收益論點

8月5日美國固定收益市場收盤，行情由先前油價帶動的漲勢轉為更具選擇性的重新定價。2年期美國公債殖利率下跌2個基點至4.18%，5年期與10年期分別持平於4.33%及4.63%，30年期則下跌1個基點至5.17%。2s10s因此走陡2個基點至45個基點，2s30s走陡1個基點至99個基點。前端承受的即時政策壓力持續消退，但較低的通膨補償遭較高的實質殖利率抵銷，加上Fed更明確反對長時間觀望，漲勢未能延伸至曲線中段。

當日核心矛盾，在於能源衝擊進一步緩解，美國國內政策反應函數卻仍偏向緊縮。伊朗表示，已與阿曼就荷姆茲海峽擬議航運路線達成協議，美國油價收在約$75。WTI再跌1.02%至$75.00，但布蘭特原油在前兩個交易日大跌後，幾乎持平於$79.33。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.22%，延續市場對航道重啟可降低短期通膨的判斷。然而，10年期實質殖利率上升1個基點至2.41%。名目殖利率收盤因此顯示，能源外交降低了通膨尾部風險，卻未降低持有中期存續期間所需的實質報酬。

Fed溝通是漲勢的主要限制。明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari是上次會議主張升息25個基點的3位異議者之一；他表示現在應開始漸進緊縮。9月是否行動仍取決於後續數據，但若通膨持平或惡化，年底前可能升息3次。堪薩斯市聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid則判斷，目前政策限制性不足，並將供給驅動型通膨升勢能否持續，連結至需求強度及Fed的回應。費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson因政策限制程度仍不確定而保持開放態度。整體而言，這些訊號擴大了偏鷹論點的支持基礎：若需求與基礎通膨未降溫，僅靠油價下跌仍不足以放鬆政策。

美國財政部再融資聲明消除了一項眼前的長端不確定性，卻未解決中長期財政問題。官員重申，名目附息債券與浮動利率票據規模至少未來數季應維持不變，將調整時點推遲至2027年相當後段。財政部也將未來發行「增加」的措辭，改為更具彈性的「調整」，同時保留一旦標售規模最終上升，將偏向較短天期的立場。下週$1,250億再融資將籌得約$287億新資金。近期規模穩定支撐長端，但本季借款預估達$7,390億，且更仰賴國庫券，使本期行事曆過後的期限溢價問題仍在。

整體信用市場維持有序，LQD近乎持平，HYG與JNK跌幅均不到0.1%。表面之下，融資承接能力仍取決於交易結構及供給集中度。Ares正主導一筆$22億收購貸款，利差至少8個百分點，顯示私人資本仍可供應，但要求的價格甚高。投資等級市場的新疑慮並非市場立即關閉，而是地域性排擠：超大規模雲端業者大量借款，已使Meta與Oracle債券利差在7月平均擴大約22及29個基點；若歐洲發行量進一步增加，可能侵蝕該區域原有的相對信用優勢。

全球及新興市場證據更支持分化，而非共同寬鬆循環。印度央行將利率維持在5.25%，並在等待通膨更廣泛傳導之際，下修10月升息定價；菲律賓與泰國整體通膨均放緩，但基礎壓力差異顯著。中國離岸主權債標售的長天期人民幣債券需求異常強勁。非洲方面，債務稽核改善與可能推進的IMF計畫，使加彭明顯有別於塞內加爾；然而，加彭私募債殖利率達12.65%，顯示償債能力預期改善尚未帶來低成本融資。因此，當日收盤是美國存續期間漲勢受控的停頓：前端利多仍在、近期供給風險下降、流動性維持，但高實質殖利率、偏鷹派的政策選擇空間及具選擇性的融資成本，使整體環境依舊緊縮。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

殖利率曲線集中呈現當日歧見。2年期殖利率下跌2個基點，5年期與10年期持平，形成小幅扭轉式走陡；30年期殖利率下跌1個基點，則使2s30s維持在接近前一週的水準。這與前一日由5至10年期帶動的漲勢不同。市場仍在下修能源衝擊，但邊際利多目前主要流向政策敏感的前端與通膨補償，而非實質存續期間。5年期與10年期恰在政策公信力與未來供給重疊程度最高的位置止漲。

觀察期間仍然關鍵。2年期殖利率較1週前低4個基點，較1個月前僅高4個基點。10年期較1週前同樣低4個基點，卻較1個月前高14個基點；30年期較1週前低3個基點，較1個月前則高19個基點。近期通膨壓力緩解，已收復7月底賣壓的一部分，但按月觀察，殖利率升幅仍隨天期拉長而擴大。這種型態持續區隔較溫和的近期政策路徑，以及市場對實質報酬、政策不確定性與財政融資所要求的持久溢價。

抗通膨債券定價進一步凸顯這項差異。10年期名目殖利率持平，是因損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.22%，正好遭實質殖利率上升1個基點至2.41%抵銷。過去1個月，損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點，實質殖利率則上升15個基點。市場並未因伊朗戰爭而在此天期計入永久較高的平均通膨率；市場要求顯著更高的實質報酬，同時隨油價與外交進展反覆調整短期通膨尾部風險。

荷姆茲海峽的進展持續壓低通膨成分，但美國公債反應遞減，反映擬議路線與實體流量正常化之間仍有落差。伊朗與阿曼正敲定該路線的聯合聲明，談判據稱持續推進。相關雙邊進展的說明並未提及美國角色。WTI續跌，布蘭特原油卻近乎持平，顯示前兩個交易日共同且大幅的能源重新定價正失去動能。對利率而言，航運安全、保險可得性及可持續的通行量，比另一則外交標題更具影響。

美國國內政策訊號則朝相反方向發展。Kashkari主張現在開始漸進升息，將先前的異議轉化為明確的當前政策建議。他對9月的疑慮並未弱化其條件：若通膨維持橫向或惡化，逐步升息即有必要，且年底前可能行動3次。因此，前端漲勢取決於數據，不能只靠外交進展。市場仍定價年底前升息1次，低於前一週的2次；2年期收盤因而反映油價反轉後的緊縮幅度下降，但並未認定升息循環已經結束。

Schmid雖然今年沒有投票權，卻擴大了支持緊縮的政策陣營。他表示，強勁需求與投資代表政策不具限制性，並主張需求穩健時，供給衝擊更容易引發通膨。他強調市場對Fed回應的預期，直接點出公信力傳導管道：能源衝擊可以在現貨市場消退，但其在薪資、服務或預期中的持續性，取決於決策官員能否抑制第二輪效應。Paulson的開放立場構成制衡，但她對政策限制性是否足夠仍不確定，意味市場仍需看到實際通膨降溫。

同日總體數據未能化解爭議。美國7月服務業活動穩定擴張，企業面臨服務與材料成本上升，招聘則弱於預期。就業轉弱降低立即緊縮的必要，持續的投入成本與具韌性的經濟活動則支持需求尚未充分轉弱的疑慮，兩種解讀各有依據。美國公債淨變動有限，與這種混合狀態一致。因此，週五政府就業報告所含的政策資訊高於單一私人招聘訊號。

債務管理消除了一項原先預期的近期衝擊。財政部至少未來數季維持名目附息債券與浮動利率票據的標售規模，符合交易商對政策延續性的預期。$1,250億再融資及$287億新資金屬已公布行事曆，而非需求結果。關鍵在於，殖利率已偏高之際，政府並未加速長天期發債。30年期殖利率下跌1個基點，符合該決策帶來的溫和緩解，但5.17%的收盤殖利率顯示利多有限。

措辭調整保留了更大的策略模糊空間。將未來「增加」改稱「調整」，可能擴大財政部選項，但官員仍維持日後若擴大發行，將偏重短端的立場。財政部借款諮詢委員會成員仍認為，預測可能支持自10月1日起的會計年度提高附息債券發行，並敦促採用保留彈性的文字。延後調整會將更多融資推向占比已處歷史高位的國庫券，並使債務利息成本對Fed重新啟動升息循環更為敏感。

利率市場的結論，是通膨降溫利多延伸至前端，但實質存續期間環境仍穩定且昂貴。損益兩平通膨率下降與附息債券規模不變，避免市場再度遭到拋售；10年期實質殖利率上升、政策官員明確呼籲收緊，以及從國庫券轉向未來附息債券的問題未解，則阻止漲勢擴大。曲線已不再按能源衝擊高峰定價，但在中長期殖利率能夠明顯跟隨前端下行前，市場仍要求美國國內通膨降溫，以及可信的長期融資安排。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

美國公債殖利率趨穩之際，整體信用價格未見系統性斷裂。LQD下跌0.02%，HYG下跌0.04%，JNK下跌0.08%。小幅波動反映總報酬大致持平，而非明確的現券利差事件。更具參考價值的，是借款人必須以何種條件才能吸引資本。市場仍然開放，但對具明確現金流的收購融資，以及用於支應資本密集度異常偏高的成長或保障不足槓桿之債務，持續採取不同定價。

私人信貸同時展現承接能力與價格紀律。Ares正主導一筆$22億直接貸款，支應MedImpact Holdings擬收購波多黎各Medical Card System；這是今年稍早創紀錄贖回干擾該產業後規模最大的交易之一。該貸款利率可能至少較基準高8個百分點。若交易以此條件完成，代表大型收購融資在聯貸市場以外仍可取得，但利差已納入相當高的門檻，借款人的營運表現仍是再融資能力核心。

投資等級供給面臨另一項限制：集中度。美國市場承接的AI基礎設施超大規模雲端業者借款比例過高，因而支撐歐洲相對估值優勢。大量發債迫使投資人賣出流通在外的Amazon債券，為該公司上月$250億發行案騰出空間。7月整體而言，Meta債券利差平均擴大約22個基點，Oracle則約29個基點。目前的新變化是，美國融資成本偏高，發行人日益轉向歐元、英鎊與瑞士法郎市場，將相同的投資組合承接壓力輸出至過去被視為較乾淨替代選項的市場。

即使發行人信用良好，這套機制仍然重要。許多超大規模雲端業者可承受額外槓桿，且相對其評等仍能以低成本借款。尚未解決的問題，是晶片、伺服器與資料中心網路能否創造與融資規模相稱的報酬。若在歐洲發債成為常態，投資組合可能必須賣出既有科技債券或其他投資等級部位來承接，導致即使近期信用指標未惡化，利差仍因供給而擴大。票息收入可緩衝報酬，但當初級市場供給持續重設次級市場估值時，無法消除按市價評價壓力。

AI投資動能也使利率與信用的界線更加複雜。市場估計2026年全球AI投資接近$1兆，其中美國略低於$6,000億；美國投資占GDP比重將由今年1.8%，升至2027年2.5%及2028年2.8%。這類支出可支撐經濟活動，並印證Schmid對需求仍強的疑慮；同時也形成龐大融資管線，與美國公債爭奪市場承接能力。同一批投資長期可能支撐營收與稅收，但對債券市場的即時影響，是供給增加及資金用途面臨更嚴格檢視。

近期初級市場證據仍不支持資本普遍短缺的看法。前一交易日AbbVie的$100億交易橫跨長天期並獲大量訂單，Baker Tilly則放棄一筆結合再融資與潛在股東股利的槓桿貸款。週三並未改變這些交易結果。新的Ares貸款將相同排序延伸至私人市場：只要貸方取得足夠利差，且資金具有明確收購用途，資本仍可供應；交易結構與價值流失則仍具決定性。

融資條件本身未在同一交易日出現裂痕。短天期國庫券殖利率沒有一致性失序，而財政部提高對國庫券的依賴，仍獲貨幣市場基金及Fed到期抵押貸款部位再投資的需求承接。脆弱點在於存續期間與利率敏感度，而非當前市場准入。未來若升息，規模更大的國庫券存量其展期成本將上升，大型公司債供給也可能同時迫使資產負債表做出配置選擇。

因此，信用市場流動性仍在，但承接能力受限。基金報酬持平，掩蓋私人收購融資成本高昂，以及投資等級資產負債表競爭升溫。真正分界不只是評等類別，而是資金用途、預期生產力、天期、契約保障及競爭性供給量。美國公債殖利率穩定，使週三基準利率負擔維持受控，卻未放寬供給集中或高槓桿借款人的成交條件。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

全球存續期間市場反映整體能源壓力緩解與國內通膨持續性之間的分歧擴大。印度央行引發最明確的市場反應。6人委員會一致決議連續第4次會議將附買回利率維持在5.25%，並維持中性立場。5年期政府公債殖利率下跌8個基點，10年期下跌3個基點至6.78%，市場隱含10月升息機率則由100%降至65%。由於央行未釋出吸收流動性的訊號，決策對前端的支撐大於長天期存續期間。

印度央行預測說明了曲線型態。央行將截至3月止年度通膨預測由5.1%下修至5%，並將截至2027年3月止年度成長預測由6.6%上修至6.7%。1月至3月當季成長已達7.8%；儘管6月通膨突破4%目標，官員仍認為物價壓力並未普遍化。然而，印度約90%原油仰賴進口，糧食播種進度落後，消費企業也正準備新一輪漲價。政策耐心建立在供給衝擊維持局部，而非需求疲弱。

東南亞數據顯示，區域政策無法採取一致回應。菲律賓通膨連續第3個月放緩至6.2%，低於6月的6.4%，也優於市場預期持平。核心通膨6個月來首次減速，披索兌美元升值0.7%至60.75。稻米通膨仍達17.1%，整體通膨也遠高於3%目標，因此在今年已升息50個基點後，央行仍準備進一步緊縮。目前的改善降低了急迫性，卻未恢復政策空間。

泰國整體通膨降溫較為明確，但基礎訊號仍不完整。7月CPI由2.42%放緩至1.95%，月指數繼6月下跌0.34%後再跌0.73%，市場原預期下跌0.2%。國內燃料價格下降是主要原因。然而，核心通膨由1.23%升至1.34%。結果支持繼續按兵不動，也顯示油價下跌的效益，但核心通膨上升警示，不應將能源帶動的整體通膨緩解視為需求全面降溫。

捷克數據在不同政策環境下，呈現相同的組成問題。整體通膨為1.7%，符合預期，且連續第2個月低於央行2%目標。然而，服務通膨由4.5%加速至4.7%，核心壓力仍接近3%。因此，利率可能維持3.75%，反映各組成相互衝突，而非毫無保留的寬鬆訊號。綜觀印度、泰國與捷克，整體通膨下降可讓央行保持耐心，前提是國內服務價格與需求仍受控。

中國市場則因長天期需求強勁而自成一格。財政部分別發行CNY10億的15年期與30年期離岸主權債，殖利率以1.99%及2.24%創歷史新低。2年期、3年期與5年期債券分別以1.27%、1.30%及1.43%完成發行，整體投標倍數達4.67倍，為去年6月以來最高。前一日中國境內10年期殖利率降至2個月低點1.71%；即使美國實質殖利率仍偏高，投資人仍接受長天期人民幣曝險。

這次標售不代表全球同步買進長天期債券，而是反映低波動，以及中國獨特的通膨、成長與匯率環境。歐洲面臨超大規模雲端業者轉向當地公司債市場發行的可能，即使主權債存續期間看來比美國公債更可預測，也會降低歐元投資等級債券的相對吸引力。日本仍受日圓支撐政策牽制，且較高的國內殖利率可能爭奪本地資金。對美國存續期間的淨影響因此好壞參半：油價回落擴大央行耐心，但國內通膨組成、海外發債及其他主權債殖利率，限制共同買盤的形成。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場債券收盤時，共同因子訊號不一。美元指數下跌0.17%至99.721，EMB卻下跌0.05%。長天期新興市場主權債指數上漲0.30%，與30年期美國公債殖利率下跌1個基點方向一致，但其月跌幅仍達2.73%。因此，美元環境放鬆仍不足以形成一致的新興市場買盤；主權國家各自的資產負債表與官方融資管道，主導更具實質意義的重新定價。

加彭是最明確的正面個別案例。由於投資人預期IMF計畫不涉及債務重整，其美元債今年已回報19.5%。IMF支持的稽核顯示，實際債務低於先前認知，協助加彭利差由1月約1,000個基點收斂至約608個基點。政府利用這項改善，透過2033年到期債券私募籌得$9.2億，預計將資金用於處理短期債務。資訊改善與天期管理已實質降低市場認知的違約風險。

融資價格使市場不能過度樂觀看待。加彭支付12.65%殖利率，是今年新興市場主權債最高水準；債券其後交易殖利率接近11.5%，仍高於同評等非洲發行人的10.7%平均值。投資人獲利了結，使該國2029年及2031年債券在週三回吐部分漲幅。最終稽核報告也尚未公布。IMF路徑提高不經債務重整即可再融資的機率，卻尚未使陷入困境的借款人轉為低成本信用。

塞內加爾的稽核傳導恰好相反。調查發現先前隱匿借款達$70億，IMF談判仍停滯，其貸款安排自2024年起即遭暫停。該國持續透過國內借款履行債務，但利差已由1月約1,000個基點擴大至1,541個基點。兩個年初困境程度相近的國家，如今市場評價截然不同，原因在於債務透明度朝相反方向變化。

這項比較也區隔美元流動性與償債能力。美元走弱與美國公債穩定可改善共同融資環境，卻無法抵銷不利的債務發現或官方計畫缺席。加彭私募交易證明，殖利率達兩位數時仍可進入市場；塞內加爾國內借款則證明，目前仍有持續償付能力。兩者皆無法取代可信的財政帳目與可持續的多邊架構。

中國離岸標售位於新興市場債務管理中較具韌性的一端，但風險類別不同。長天期殖利率創新低且投標倍數達4.67倍，顯示人民幣主權長天期債券需求充沛。加彭與塞內加爾則取決於硬通貨殖利率、財政透明度及IMF參與三者交互作用。整體新興市場結論是，美元溫和走弱可支撐市場運作，但主權債結果主要由資訊品質、再融資架構及官方支持決定，而非美國利率單日變動。

## 跨資產

跨資產表現反映風險資產快速上漲後進入整理，而非全面避險。S&P 500下跌0.17%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.83%，半導體指數下跌1.40%。Nasdaq 100此前4天上漲9.3%，市值增加約$3.5兆，之後賣壓集中於長存續期間股票。漲後暫歇與5年期、10年期美國公債殖利率持平相符，不能視為新的成長衝擊。

儘管股市下跌，VIX仍下滑4.18%至15.81，不支持近期股票避險需求普遍升高的判斷。SpaceX在$1,010億股票解禁前下跌14%，加上晶片製造商走弱，帶來更具個別性的壓力。整體表現顯示科技股內部的部位與估值動能耗盡，而非融資壓力引發跨資產清算。對信用市場而言，這項差異很重要：即使整體波動率與高收益債基金價格仍受控，AI融資供給仍可能推寬科技債利差。

能源持續證實即時通膨動能減弱，但力度不及前兩個交易日。WTI下跌1.02%至$75.00，布蘭特原油則幾乎持平於$79.33。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點，方向與油價一致；10年期名目殖利率持平，則顯示較高的實質補償吸收了這項利多。美元指數下跌0.17%，對全球流動性提供溫和支撐，卻未能避免整體新興市場與美國信用基金小幅下跌。

黃金是單純正常化敘事的最強反證。即使油價維持在外交進展後的低點附近，VIX也下降，黃金期貨仍大漲5.54%至$4,322.10。中國機構需求先前已支撐金價突破$4,000，本次飆升顯示，市場仍重視防範地緣政治反轉、匯率不確定性或Fed公信力風險。跨資產因此證實即時能源風險降低且流動性有序，卻也保留大量避險需求，同時對科技股領漲地位與實質存續期間估值提出質疑。

## 前瞻市場意義

週五7月就業報告將決定前端漲勢能否超越能源利多而延續。關鍵條件是私人招聘轉弱能否獲得確認，且薪資或服務壓力不再升高，因為週三服務業數據同時顯示活動穩定與投入成本上升。若就業轉弱且成本壓力下降，2年期殖利率將有空間跟隨損益兩平通膨率下行，也可能帶動5年期殖利率跌破4.33%。若招聘穩健、成本僵固，或失業數據顯示產能仍緊，將印證Kashkari的漸進升息主張及Schmid對政策不具限制性的判斷；即使原油維持約$75，政策溢價仍會重建。

荷姆茲海峽進程必須由伊朗與阿曼的路線協議，推進至安全且可投保的航運。最終協議、可持續停火及明顯的通行正常化，將使油價與損益兩平通膨率降幅更為持久，減輕從印度到東南亞的輸入性通膨壓力，並降低同步緊縮的必要。若第三方阻撓、航運威脅再起，或未能建立安全與治理安排，能源尾部風險將重新進入Fed前端定價。若原油反彈並伴隨損益兩平通膨率上升，將直接挑戰目前的通膨降溫判斷；若實質殖利率也上升，則代表公信力衝擊再起。

下週$1,250億美國公債再融資及下一波大型企業融資，將區隔溫和指引與實際承接。標售結果必須顯示，附息債券規模不變可在沒有重大讓利下順利成交；超大規模雲端業者發債則須顯示，投資組合能否在不拋售美國與歐洲市場既有債券下承接科技供給。美國公債需求有序且次級信用市場表現穩定，可使未來由「增加」改為「調整」的措辭維持為遙遠的彈性訊號。若標售需求疲弱、AI借款人利差再度擴大，或更多私人交易要求接近8個百分點的利差，限制便會由未來供給提前反映至當前成交價格。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 5 U.S. fixed-income close marked a transition from the preceding oil-led rally into a more selective repricing. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.18%, the 5- and 10-year yields held at 4.33% and 4.63%, and the 30-year eased 1 basis point to 5.17%. That left 2s10s 2 basis points steeper at 45 and 2s30s 1 basis point steeper at 99. Immediate policy pressure continued to recede at the front end, but the rally could not extend through the belly because lower inflation compensation was offset by a firmer real yield and more explicit Fed resistance to prolonged patience.

The day's central tension was between further relief from the energy shock and a domestic reaction function that remains biased toward restraint. Iran said it had reached agreement with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, and U.S. oil settled around $75. WTI fell another 1.02% to $75.00, though Brent was almost unchanged at $79.33 after the large declines of the previous two sessions. The 10-year breakeven slipped 1 basis point to 2.22%, extending the judgment that a reopening could reduce near-term inflation. The 10-year real yield, however, rose 1 basis point to 2.41%. The nominal close therefore says energy diplomacy lowered the inflation tail without reducing the real return required to own intermediate duration.

Fed communication supplied the principal limit. Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, one of the three dissenters who favored a 25-basis-point increase at the previous meeting, said tightening should begin incrementally now. He left September contingent on incoming data but said three increases by year-end were possible if inflation stayed sideways or worsened. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid separately judged current policy insufficiently restrictive, linking the persistence of a supply-driven inflation burst to the strength of demand and to the Fed's response. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson retained an open mind because the degree of restraint remains uncertain. Together, those signals broadened the argument that lower oil is insufficient if demand and underlying inflation fail to cool.

Treasury's refunding statement removed one immediate source of long-end uncertainty without resolving the fiscal horizon. Officials repeated that nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes should remain steady for at least several quarters, pushing changes well into 2027. The department also replaced a reference to future issuance “increases” with the more flexible word “changes,” while retaining a bias toward shorter maturities if auction sizes eventually rise. Next week's $125 billion refunding will raise about $28.7 billion of new cash. Stable near-term sizes supported the long end, but a $739 billion current-quarter borrowing estimate and heavier reliance on bills preserved the term-premium question beyond the current calendar.

Credit remained orderly at the aggregate level, with LQD nearly unchanged and HYG and JNK down less than 0.1%. Beneath that surface, financing capacity continued to depend on structure and concentration. Ares was leading a $2.2 billion acquisition loan at a spread of at least 8 percentage points, showing that private capital remained available at a demanding price. In investment grade, the new concern was geographic displacement rather than immediate market closure: heavy hyperscaler borrowing had already widened Meta and Oracle bond spreads by about 22 and 29 basis points on average in July, and additional issuance in Europe could erode the region's relative credit advantage.

Global and emerging-market evidence reinforced dispersion rather than a common easing cycle. India's central bank held at 5.25% and reduced October hike pricing as it waited for broader inflation pass-through, while Philippine and Thai headline inflation slowed with sharply different underlying pressures. China's offshore sovereign auction drew exceptional demand for long yuan duration. In Africa, an improved debt audit and prospective IMF program separated Gabon sharply from Senegal, but Gabon's 12.65% private-placement yield showed that better solvency expectations had not produced inexpensive funding. The close was therefore a controlled pause in the U.S. duration rally: front-end relief survived, immediate supply risk diminished, and liquidity held, but high real yields, hawkish policy optionality and selective financing costs kept the broader regime restrictive.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The curve localized the session's disagreement. A 2-basis-point decline at 2 years against unchanged 5- and 10-year yields produced a small twist steepening, while the 1-basis-point rally at 30 years left 2s30s near the prior week's level. This differed from the prior close's 5- to 10-year-led rally. The energy shock was still being marked down, but the marginal benefit now accrued mainly to the policy-sensitive front end and inflation compensation rather than to real duration. The 5-year and 10-year sectors stopped rallying exactly where policy credibility and future supply have their greatest overlap.

The horizon remains important. The 2-year yield was 4 basis points lower over 1 week and only 4 basis points higher over 1 month. The 10-year was also 4 basis points lower over the week, yet 14 basis points higher over the month; the 30-year was 3 basis points lower over the week and 19 basis points higher over the month. Near-term inflation relief has reversed part of the late-July selloff, but the rise in yields still increases with maturity over the monthly window. That profile continues to separate a softer immediate policy path from a durable premium for real returns, policy uncertainty and fiscal financing.

Inflation-linked pricing sharpened that distinction. The 10-year nominal yield was unchanged because a 1-basis-point decline in breakevens to 2.22% was offset by a 1-basis-point rise in the real yield to 2.41%. Over 1 month, the breakeven was 1 basis point lower while the real yield was 15 basis points higher. The market has not responded to the Iran war by embedding a permanently higher average inflation rate at this horizon. It has demanded a substantially higher real return while repeatedly adjusting the near-term inflation tail with oil and diplomacy.

The Hormuz development kept the inflation component moving lower, but the diminishing Treasury response reflects the gap between a proposed route and normalized physical flows. Iran and Oman were finalizing a joint statement on the route, with the talks described as moving forward. No U.S. role was specified in the account of that bilateral step. WTI's additional decline contrasted with nearly unchanged Brent, suggesting that the large common energy repricing of the prior two sessions was losing force. Shipping security, insurance availability and durable throughput remain more consequential for rates than another diplomatic headline.

Domestic policy signals moved in the opposite direction. Kashkari's call for incremental increases now converted his earlier dissent into an explicit current prescription. His uncertainty about September did not dilute the condition: if inflation remains sideways or worsens, gradual increases become necessary, and three moves before year-end are possible. That keeps the front-end rally conditional on data rather than on diplomacy alone. Markets still priced one increase by year-end, down from two the previous week, so the 2-year close reflects less tightening than before the oil reversal but not an abandoned hiking cycle.

Schmid widened the policy coalition even though he does not vote this year. He said strong demand and investment meant policy was not restrictive and argued that supply shocks are more inflationary when demand is firm. His emphasis on the expected Fed response identifies the credibility channel directly: an energy shock can fade in spot markets while its persistence in wages, services or expectations depends on whether policymakers contain second-round effects. Paulson's open-minded stance supplies the counterweight, but her uncertainty about whether policy is restrictive enough leaves the burden on realized disinflation.

The same-day macro account did not resolve that dispute. U.S. services activity expanded at a steady pace in July, firms faced rising costs for services and materials, and hiring was weaker than expected. The combination offers each side partial support: softer employment reduces the need for immediate restraint, whereas persistent input costs and resilient activity validate concern that demand has not weakened enough. The limited net Treasury move is consistent with that mixed state. Friday's government employment release therefore carries more policy information than the private hiring signal alone.

Debt management removed an anticipated near-term shock. Treasury maintained auction sizes for nominal coupons and floating-rate notes for at least several quarters, matching the continuity expected by dealers. The $125 billion refunding and $28.7 billion of new cash are an announced calendar, not a demand result. Their significance is that the government did not accelerate long-duration issuance when yields were already elevated. The 30-year's 1-basis-point rally is consistent with modest relief from that decision, though its 5.17% close shows the relief was limited.

The wording change preserves a larger strategic ambiguity. Referring to future “changes” instead of “increases” could widen Treasury's options, but officials retained the short-end bias for any eventual expansion. Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee members still judged that projections could warrant higher coupon issuance in the fiscal year beginning October 1 and urged language that preserves flexibility. Delaying the adjustment pushes more financing into bills, whose share is already historically high, and makes debt-service costs more sensitive to a renewed Fed hiking cycle.

The rates conclusion is a front-end extension of disinflation relief against a stable, expensive real-duration regime. Lower breakevens and unchanged coupon sizes prevented a renewed selloff. A higher 10-year real yield, explicit calls for tighter policy and the unresolved migration from bills to future coupons prevented a broader rally. The curve is no longer pricing the oil shock at its peak, but it still requires domestic disinflation and credible long-horizon financing before intermediate and long yields can follow the front end materially lower.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit prices showed no systemic break as Treasury yields stabilized. LQD fell 0.02%, HYG declined 0.04% and JNK lost 0.08%. Their small moves indicate a flat total-return session rather than a clear cash-spread event. More useful evidence came from the terms on which borrowers could attract capital. The market remained open, but it continued to distinguish acquisition financing with identifiable cash flows from debt used to fund unusually capital-intensive growth or weakly protected leverage.

Private credit demonstrated both capacity and price discipline. Ares was leading a $2.2 billion direct loan to finance MedImpact Holdings' planned acquisition of Puerto Rico-based Medical Card System, one of the largest transactions since record redemptions disrupted the sector earlier in the year. The loan could pay at least 8 percentage points over its benchmark. Completion at that level would show that large acquisition funding remains available outside syndicated markets, but the spread embeds a substantial hurdle and leaves the borrower's operating performance central to refinancing capacity.

Investment-grade supply faces a different constraint: concentration. U.S. markets have carried a disproportionate share of hyperscaler borrowing for AI infrastructure, supporting Europe's relative valuation advantage. Heavy issuance forced investors to sell outstanding Amazon bonds to create room for the company's $25 billion offering last month. Across July, Meta's bonds widened about 22 basis points on average and Oracle's about 29. The current delta is that issuers are increasingly tapping euros, sterling and Swiss francs because U.S. funding is expensive, exporting the same portfolio-capacity pressure into markets previously viewed as cleaner alternatives.

That mechanism matters even for strong issuers. Many hyperscalers can support additional leverage and still borrow cheaply relative to their ratings. The unresolved question is whether chips, servers and data-center networks generate returns commensurate with the financing scale. If issuance becomes systematic in Europe, portfolios may have to sell existing technology bonds or other investment-grade holdings to absorb it, widening spreads through supply even without deterioration in near-term credit metrics. Yield income can cushion returns, but it does not eliminate mark-to-market pressure when primary volume continually resets secondary valuations.

The AI investment impulse also complicates the rates-credit boundary. Estimates place 2026 global AI investment near $1 trillion, including just under $600 billion in the U.S., with the U.S. share rising from 1.8% of GDP this year to 2.5% in 2027 and 2.8% in 2028. That spending can sustain activity and validate Schmid's concern that demand remains strong. It also creates a large financing pipeline whose absorption competes with Treasury issuance. The same investment may support revenues and tax receipts over time, but its immediate bond-market effect is more supply and greater scrutiny of proceeds.

Recent primary-market evidence still argues against a generalized shortage of capital. The prior session's $10 billion AbbVie transaction cleared across a long maturity range with a large orderbook, whereas Baker Tilly abandoned a leveraged loan that combined refinancing with a potential sponsor dividend. Wednesday did not change those transaction outcomes. The new Ares loan extends the same hierarchy into private markets: capital is available when lenders receive enough spread and a defined acquisition purpose, while structure and value leakage remain decisive.

Funding conditions themselves did not display a same-session fracture. Short bill yields showed no coherent dislocation, and Treasury's increased reliance on bills has continued to meet demand from money-market funds and the Fed's reinvestment of maturing mortgage holdings. The vulnerability lies in duration and rate sensitivity rather than current market access. A future policy increase would raise the cost of rolling a larger bill stock, and large corporate issuance could force balance-sheet allocation choices at the same time.

Credit therefore remains liquid but capacity-constrained. Flat fund returns mask expensive private acquisition finance and growing competition for investment-grade balance sheets. The decisive fault line is not simply rating category. It runs through use of proceeds, expected productivity, maturity, covenant protection and the volume of competing supply. Stable Treasury yields kept the benchmark burden contained on Wednesday; they did not relax the clearing terms for concentrated or highly leveraged borrowers.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Global duration reflected a widening divergence between headline energy relief and domestic inflation persistence. India's central bank provided the clearest market reaction. The six-member committee unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% for a fourth meeting and retained a neutral stance. Five-year government yields fell 8 basis points and the 10-year declined 3 basis points to 6.78%, while the market-implied probability of an October increase dropped to 65% from 100%. Absent a signal that liquidity would be absorbed, the decision delivered more relief to the front end than to long duration.

The RBI's forecasts explain the shape. It lowered inflation for the year through March to 5% from 5.1% and raised growth for the year ending March 2027 to 6.7% from 6.6%. Growth had reached 7.8% in the January-March quarter, and officials saw little generalization of price pressure despite a June breach of the 4% inflation target. Yet India imports roughly 90% of its crude, food planting has lagged, and consumer companies were preparing another round of price increases. Patience rests on the supply shock remaining narrow, not on weak demand.

Southeast Asian releases showed why the regional policy response cannot be uniform. Philippine inflation slowed for a third month to 6.2%, below both June's 6.4% and expectations for no change. Core inflation decelerated for the first time in six months, and the peso strengthened 0.7% to 60.75 per dollar. Rice inflation at 17.1% and a headline rate far above the 3% target still kept the central bank prepared to tighten after 50 basis points of increases this year. The current improvement reduced urgency without restoring policy space.

Thailand offered cleaner headline disinflation but a less complete underlying signal. July CPI slowed to 1.95% from 2.42%, and the monthly index fell 0.73% after a 0.34% decline in June, compared with an expected 0.2% drop. Lower domestic fuel prices supplied the main mechanism. Core inflation nevertheless rose to 1.34% from 1.23%. The result supports a continued hold and demonstrates the benefit of lower oil, but the core move cautions against treating energy-driven headline relief as broad demand disinflation.

The Czech release carried the same composition problem in a different policy setting. Headline inflation was 1.7%, matching expectations and undershooting the central bank's 2% target for a second month. Services inflation accelerated to 4.7% from 4.5%, however, while core pressure remained near 3%. A likely hold at 3.75% would therefore reflect conflicting components rather than an unqualified easing signal. Across India, Thailand and the Czech Republic, lower headline inflation allows patience only while domestic services and demand remain contained.

China stood apart through outright demand for duration. The Ministry of Finance sold CNY1 billion each of 15- and 30-year offshore sovereign bonds at record-low yields of 1.99% and 2.24%. Two-, three- and five-year notes cleared at 1.27%, 1.30% and 1.43%, and the overall bid-to-cover ratio reached 4.67, the highest since June last year. With China's onshore 10-year yield at a two-month low of 1.71% the previous day, investors accepted long yuan exposure even as U.S. real yields remained elevated.

That auction does not imply a synchronized global duration bid. It reflects low volatility and China's distinct inflation, growth and currency regime. Europe faces the possibility that hyperscaler issuance migrates into its corporate markets, reducing the relative appeal of euro investment grade even if sovereign duration looks more predictable than Treasuries. Japan remains tied to yen support and the prospect that higher domestic yields compete for local capital. The net implication for U.S. duration is mixed: oil relief broadens central-bank patience, but domestic inflation composition, foreign issuance and alternative sovereign yields limit a common buyer-base response.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt ended with mixed common-factor signals. The Dollar Index fell 0.17% to 99.721, yet EMB slipped 0.05%. The long-duration EM sovereign index gained 0.30%, consistent with the 1-basis-point rally in the 30-year Treasury, but its monthly loss remained 2.73%. Easier dollar conditions were therefore insufficient to create a uniform EM bid. Sovereign-specific balance sheets and access to official funding dominated the more consequential repricing.

Gabon supplied the clearest positive idiosyncratic case. Its dollar bonds had returned 19.5% this year as investors anticipated an IMF program without restructuring. An IMF-supported audit indicated lower debt than previously understood, helping compress Gabon's spread to about 608 basis points from roughly 1,000 in January. The government used that improvement to raise $920 million privately through a bond maturing in 2033, with proceeds expected to address short-term obligations. Better information and maturity management materially reduced perceived default risk.

The price of that access prevents an overly benign reading. Gabon paid 12.65%, the highest yield for an emerging sovereign this year, and the bond later traded near 11.5%, still above the 10.7% average for similarly rated African issuers. Its 2029 and 2031 bonds gave back part of their rally on Wednesday as investors took profit. The final audit has also yet to be released. An IMF path improves the probability of refinancing without restructuring, but it has not converted a distressed borrower into low-cost credit.

Senegal shows the opposite audit transmission. Its investigation uncovered $7 billion of previously hidden borrowing, IMF talks remained stalled and its lending facility has been suspended since 2024. The sovereign has continued servicing obligations through domestic borrowing, yet its spread widened to 1,541 basis points from about 1,000 in January. Two countries that began the year at similar distress levels now carry radically different market judgments because debt transparency changed in opposite directions.

The comparison also separates dollar liquidity from solvency. A softer dollar and stable Treasuries can improve the common funding backdrop, but they cannot offset an adverse debt discovery or the absence of an official program. Gabon's private placement proves transaction access at a double-digit yield; Senegal's domestic borrowing proves continued payment capacity for now. Neither mechanism removes the need for credible fiscal accounts and a durable multilateral framework.

China's offshore auction sits at the resilient end of EM debt management, though it belongs to a different risk class. Record-low long-maturity yields and a 4.67 bid-to-cover ratio show abundant demand for sovereign yuan duration. Gabon and Senegal instead depend on the interaction of hard-currency yields, fiscal transparency and IMF engagement. The broader EM conclusion is that a modestly weaker dollar can support market function, but sovereign outcomes are being set by information quality, refinancing architecture and official sponsorship more than by one day of U.S. rates.

## Cross asset

Cross assets depict consolidation after a rapid risk rally rather than a broad flight from risk. The S&P 500 fell 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.83% and the semiconductor index lost 1.40%. The weakness was concentrated in the long-duration equity complex after the Nasdaq 100 had gained 9.3% over four days and roughly $3.5 trillion in market value. A pause after that move is compatible with unchanged 5- and 10-year Treasury yields; it does not identify a new growth shock.

The VIX fell 4.18% to 15.81 despite lower equities, which argues against a generalized demand for near-term equity protection. SpaceX's 14% drop ahead of a $101 billion share unlock and weakness among chipmakers provided more specific pressure. The combination suggests position and valuation exhaustion inside technology rather than a funding-driven liquidation across assets. That distinction matters for credit because AI financing supply can widen technology bonds even when broad volatility and high-yield fund prices remain contained.

Energy continued to confirm a smaller immediate inflation impulse, though with less force than on the prior two sessions. WTI fell 1.02% to $75.00, while Brent was almost unchanged at $79.33. The 1-basis-point decline in the 10-year breakeven tracked that direction, and the unchanged nominal 10-year yield shows that rising real compensation absorbed the benefit. The Dollar Index's 0.17% decline added mild support to global liquidity but did not prevent small losses in broad EM and U.S. credit funds.

Gold was the strongest contradiction to a simple normalization narrative. Futures rose 5.54% to $4,322.10 even as oil held near its post-diplomacy lows and the VIX declined. Chinese institutional demand had already supported bullion above $4,000, and the current surge indicates that protection against geopolitical reversal, currency uncertainty or Fed credibility remained valuable. Cross assets therefore confirm lower immediate energy risk and orderly liquidity, yet they also preserve a substantial demand for hedges while technology leadership and real-duration valuations are being questioned.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's July employment report determines whether the front-end rally can extend beyond energy relief. The relevant condition is whether weaker private hiring is confirmed without renewed wage or services pressure, since Wednesday's services account combined steady activity with rising input costs. Softer employment alongside lower cost pressure would give the 2-year room to follow breakevens lower and could pull the 5-year off 4.33%. Firm hiring, sticky costs or an unemployment result that leaves capacity tight would validate Kashkari's incremental-hike case and Schmid's judgment that policy is not restrictive, rebuilding the policy premium even if crude remains near $75.

The Hormuz process must progress from an Iran-Oman route agreement to secure, insurable shipping. A finalized arrangement, durable ceasefire and visible normalization of traffic would make the decline in oil and breakevens more persistent, reducing imported-inflation pressure from India to Southeast Asia and narrowing the need for synchronized tightening. Obstruction by third parties, renewed shipping threats or failure to establish security and governance would put the energy tail back into front-end Fed pricing. A reversal in crude accompanied by higher breakevens would directly challenge the current disinflation interpretation; higher real yields as well would signal a renewed credibility shock.

Next week's $125 billion Treasury refunding and the next wave of large corporate financing separate benign guidance from actual absorption. Auction results must show that steady coupon sizes can clear without a material concession, while hyperscaler issuance must show whether portfolios can absorb technology supply without selling outstanding bonds across U.S. and European markets. Orderly Treasury demand and stable secondary credit performance would allow the wording change from future “increases” to “changes” to remain a distant flexibility signal. Weak auction demand, renewed widening around AI borrowers or additional private deals requiring spreads near 8 percentage points would move the constraint from future supply into current clearing prices.
